independentAdversarialProbes.method: Deep-copy the reviewed JSON in memory, mutate one semantic obligation at a time, invoke the retained checker function, and preserve the repository files unchanged.

probes.mutation: Create two logical evaluation tuples whose components contain U+001F so both serialize to 61 1f 62 1f 63, then recompute all declared commitments.
probes.expected: A complete-universe commitment must distinguish distinct logical evaluations or the identifier grammar must reject the delimiter.
probes.observed: Both logical tuples have identical item bytes and identical commitments; the full evaluation-proof checker accepts the two-evaluation positive vector with no findings.

probes.mutation: Change a match bundle with an empty waiver set to verdict=pass.
probes.expected: The verdict must be derived from the complete outcome, baseline, waiver, and policy state.

probes.mutation: Use outcome=partial-but-treated-clean, claimShape=future-unverified-shape, an empty proof, and verdict=pass; recompute commitments.
probes.expected: Unknown outcome and proof-shape variants must be rejected before verdict derivation.
probes.observed: Accepted with no findings because the unknown shape bypasses every proof-specific branch.

probes.mutation: Delete requiredUniverse.memberIds from a retained positive vector.
probes.expected: A field presented as the exact declared member set must be required and checked or removed from the binding shape.
probes.observed: Accepted with no findings; the field is not read.

probes.mutation: Append an accepting closure with proofRefs=[], units=[], sealedCapability=verifiable, and expectedEffectiveCapability=verifiable.
probes.expected: A verifiable capability cannot be established by an empty proof dependency closure.
probes.observed: Accepted with no findings. check-retention-custody.py declares PROOF=evaluation-proof.v1.json, but its check function never reads that constant or the proof graph.

probes.mutation: Delete proofRefs from accepted CL-POS-01 while leaving its units and expected capability unchanged.
probes.expected: Every proof dependency must remain joined to exactly one retained unit.

probes.mutation: Relabel a unit needed by a verifiable claim as requiredForCapability=recorded and recompute the closure commitment.
probes.expected: The claimed exact minimum capability must be equality-checked against the proof dependency.
probes.observed: Accepted with no findings; the checker rejects only one inequality direction.

probes.mutation: Replace the atomicity sentence with 'NOT ONE transaction; resolve first and pin later'.
probes.expected: A split resolve/pin operation must be rejected.
probes.observed: Accepted with no findings because the text still contains the token ONE.

probes.mutation: Replace the lease-record field list with the single field isPinned.
probes.expected: A durable lease needs closed identity, owner, scope, state, expiry, and fencing material rather than a boolean surrogate.

probes.observed: Accepted with no findings; retention compares only errorCode or reasonCodes[0] and drops the second derived reason code.

probes.expected: The reused D9 scenario-axis schema must be exact and closed.
The candidate's no-premature-resolution guard must reject any positive resolution claim before independent review and product disposition.

priorFindingRepairAssessment.summary: 0 PASS / 7 FAIL under adversarial semantic review. Several live candidate statements are improved and honest, but no prior finding is closed at the required checker-and-integration assurance level.

findings.title: The canonical commitment grammar is non-injective across tuple components
evidence: R8-P1A-P01 constructs distinct member tuples (a, b\u001fc) and (a\u001fb, c) that both encode as hex 611f621f63.
Distinct outcome tuples likewise both encode as 611f621f631f64.
The grammar length-prefixes only the already-concatenated item; it does not frame each logical component, and the accepted schema does not exclude U+001F from identifiers.
The checker accepts a positive vector containing the colliding logical evaluations because set deduplication occurs after ambiguous tuple serialization.
findings.impact: A universe or outcome-set commitment can claim two distinct logical evaluations while cryptographically committing to one byte member. Exact activation and complete outcome coverage are therefore not established.
findings.falsifier: Show a binding, closed identifier grammar consumed by every producer and checker that rejects U+001F before commitment, or demonstrate component-wise length-prefixing/type-tagging that gives the two probe tuples different bytes and commitments.
findings.requiredChange: Version the byte grammar and encode each tuple component with its own type tag and length, or bind and validate a delimiter-excluding identifier grammar. Add independently authored member and outcome collision negatives and cross-language golden bytes.

findings.title: Open proof/outcome/verdict domains let unknown evidence bypass verification and let an unsupported clean verdict pass
evidence: R8-P1A-P02 changes a match with no waivers to verdict=pass and is accepted.
R8-P1A-P03 supplies an unknown outcome, unknown claimShape, empty proof, and pass verdict; recomputed commitments are accepted.
R8-P1A-P04 removes requiredUniverse.memberIds and is accepted.
The checker recomputes identifier sets but does not execute a closed policy/verdict derivation over baseline, waivers, outcomes, and historical policy semantics.
findings.impact: A Run can be marked verifiable and clean even though its outcome kind has no proof obligation or its verdict is not justified by the committed outcome set.
findings.falsifier: A closed schema and independent oracle reject all three probes and recompute verdict from retained, versioned policy/baseline/waiver semantics rather than comparing an asserted verdict string.
findings.requiredChange: Close Evaluation, outcome, claimShape, proof-union, and verdict schemas; reject unknown variants and undeclared keys; define and execute verdict derivation; either validate declared memberIds exactly or remove it from the binding contract. Add unknown-enum, match-to-pass, omitted-member-list, and proof-union negatives.

findings.title: Capability closure is not derived from the authoritative evaluation-proof object graph
evidence: R8-P1A-P05 accepts a verifiable closure containing zero proof references and zero units.
R8-P1A-P06 deletes proofRefs from an accepted positive fixture without rejection.
R8-P1A-P07 weakens a verifiable dependency's claimed exact minimum to recorded and is accepted.
check-retention-custody.py declares evaluation-proof.v1.json as PROOF, but the check function does not read that constant or join the proof object's references.
findings.impact: Omitted or misclassified proof dependencies can leave effectiveCapability=verifiable after the material needed to verify the Run is absent.
findings.falsifier: The retention checker loads a concrete evaluation-proof bundle, derives its complete reference set and exact per-reference minimum capability, and rejects the empty, omitted-reference, duplicate-alias, and both-direction minimum mutations.
findings.requiredChange: Define a sealed host-owned closure derivation over the exact evaluation and verdict proof graph. Make proofRefs derived, non-vacuous for verifiable claims, bijective to retained units where required, and equality-check requiredForCapability. Add end-to-end cross-artifact fixtures rather than self-contained closure examples.

findings.title: Lease fixtures do not make atomicity, identity, crash recovery, or non-preemption load-bearing
evidence: R8-P1A-P08 accepts an atomicity sentence that explicitly says resolve and pin are not one transaction.
R8-P1A-P09 accepts a one-field boolean lease surrogate.
R8-P1A-P10 accepts a crashed lease held forever when prose and expected state are edited together.
R8-P1A-P11 accepts expiry preemption of a live reader when prose and expected row are edited together.
findings.impact: The retained green suite cannot distinguish the intended TOCTOU closure from materially unsafe lease protocols. Implementers can follow an accepted mutated contract and reintroduce purge/read races or unrecoverable locks.
findings.falsifier: A closed transition reducer independently derives every fixture result from typed lease state and rejects the four probes without substring matching or trusting fixture expectations.
findings.requiredChange: Represent lease identity, scope, owner, fencing token, state, expiry, and transaction boundary as closed fields. Implement a normative transition function covering resolve-and-pin, purge ordering, release, crash reclaim, expiry during use, and D9 outcomes; make fixtures inputs to that function.

findings.title: Retention purge validation is not joined to ProjectId storage lineage
evidence: The base retention purge fixtures contain no ProjectId on the purge request or objects.
R8-P1A-P12 explicitly assigns the request and removed object to different ProjectIds; the retention checker accepts removal.
threat-model.v3 separately specifies PROJECT-ID-V1 lexical and physical namespaces, but retention validation does not consume that ownership relation.
findings.impact: The same green retention suite can describe a cross-project deletion, contradicting the storage namespace and isolation contract that targeted purge relies on.
findings.falsifier: Every purge request, unit, object, pin, Run, and lineage edge carries a validated ProjectId and an independent cross-artifact check rejects cross-project traversal/removal while preserving blocked-shared-object behavior.
findings.requiredChange: Join purge semantics to the PROJECT-ID-V1 owner and storage namespace. Add exact ProjectId fields and referential constraints to fixtures, forbid cross-project object/ref/pin edges, and add equal-digest cross-project and malicious-lineage negatives.

findings.title: The retention-to-D9 join validates only a primary projection, not the closed scenario and full derived result
evidence: R8-P1A-P13 adds a valid secondary deficiency so D9 derives a second reason code; retention silently drops it and passes.
R8-P1A-P14 adds an undeclared nested axis and passes.
The positive control confirms an incorrect primary class is rejected, so the gap is specifically incomplete payload and schema validation rather than no D9 join at all.
findings.impact: Callers can receive an incomplete remediation payload, and undeclared axes can change meaning outside D9's reviewed contract while RC-10 remains green.
findings.falsifier: Retention validates rows against D9's exact scenario-axis schema and compares the complete derived class, errorCode, ordered reasonCodes, and any other normative output; both probes reject.
findings.requiredChange: Reuse or export D9's closed input/output schemas, reject missing/extra/type-confused axes, and compare the complete derive_codes result rather than errorCode or reasonCodes[0]. Add multi-deficiency and undeclared-axis fixtures.

findings.title: Product and integration authority remain contradictory and the no-self-sign guards are open-shape bypassable
evidence: The live plan, threat model, product disposition, and v6 correctly say Phase 1A OPEN, V10 UNRESOLVED, and CD-RT-5 BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A.
architecture/06 lines 158-165 and 274-275 still say v5 closes V10 and cite evidence.v1; architecture/09 lines 42 and 48 repeat V10 resolved, v5 binding, and product posture signed.
claim-register.v1 lines 915 and 950-974 still say v5 closes V10, names v5 as binding, records CD-RT-5 SIGNED OFF, and lists CD-RT-5 and V10 as resolved.

R8-P1A-P15..P17 show that v6 currentState=RESOLVED, a nested resolves declaration, and a nested productAcceptance=ACCEPTED self-sign all pass the applicable checkers; the self-sign passes both retention and product checks.
findings.impact: Readers and automation can select a stale authoritative-looking file that treats an expressly blocked product decision as accepted. The candidate checker cannot guarantee that architecture did not manufacture product authority or prematurely close V10.
findings.falsifier: At one hashed snapshot every binding/restating consumer agrees on v6 pending state, and closed schemas plus a live product-authority cross-read reject every positive resolution/acceptance claim outside the product-owned transition.
findings.requiredChange: Keep CD-RT-5 product-owned and blocked. Close v6's authority/integration object schemas; forbid resolution or acceptance semantically at every path; update the product checker to understand the v6 shape; then, in a separately authorized serialized integration, replace stale v5/evidence.v1 and signed/resolved claims across architecture/06, architecture/09, claim-register, TM, operability, and completeness state. Do not perform that integration until architecture re-review passes and product records CD-RT-5.

findings.title: All five retained checkers can raise uncaught exceptions on hostile nested types
evidence: R8-P1A-P18 supplies a boolean where each checker expects an object: evaluation, D9, threat, and product raise AttributeError; retention raises TypeError.
A nested dictionary in partitionContents also reaches set construction and raises TypeError rather than EP findings.
findings.impact: Malformed or adversarial review artifacts produce traceback-shaped failure rather than deterministic typed validation, weakening totality claims and making automation distinguish parser crashes from semantic rejection.
findings.falsifier: Every JSON value accepted by the parser yields a finite finding list and controlled nonzero process result across all five checkers, including nested scalar/container substitutions.
findings.requiredChange: Validate container and scalar types before access, close nested schemas, catch validation-boundary exceptions, and add systematic hostile-type/selftest matrices for every object, array, string, boolean, and null position.

sealRecommendation.reason: CD-RT-5 remains a necessary product-owned gate, but it is not the only gate. Eight open findings include three critical proof/closure defects, a critical authority/integration contradiction, and high-severity lease, purge-lineage, and D9 gaps.
minimumBeforeReReview: Make the commitment tuple grammar injective and publish independent cross-language collision goldens.
Close evaluation/proof/outcome/verdict schemas and make verdict derivation executable from retained semantics.
Derive capability closure from the actual evaluation-proof graph with exact minima.
Replace lease token/presence checks with a closed normative transition reducer.
Join purge lineage to ProjectId and retention D9 rows to D9's full closed input/output contract.
Make all five checkers total on hostile JSON shapes.
After those repairs pass independent re-review, let product separately decide CD-RT-5 and only then perform one serialized integration update.

knownLimitations: This is an architecture/contract and checker review, not a storage benchmark, cryptographic audit, runtime race demonstration, or product qualification.

The independent commitment oracle recomputed the published vectors and framing behavior; it did not claim collision resistance beyond SHA-256's ordinary assumption. The reported collision is in tuple serialization before hashing, not a SHA-256 collision.

Accepted in-memory mutations prove missing enforcement. Except for the separately enumerated stale integration files, they do not claim that the current candidate literally contains the mutated unsafe text.
No product disposition is created or inferred by this review. CD-RT-5 remains exclusively product-owned and blocked.
No prior finding is self-adjudicated by this reviewer; all R8-P1A findings remain OPEN for repair and later independent verification.
